tagline: Abidjan on the Ébrié Lagoon — West Africa's great lagoon city, where boats already move the commute and the government is electrifying the water.
summary: Côte d'Ivoire's marine-mobility heart is Abidjan, built around the vast sheltered Ébrié Lagoon that separates the business district of Le Plateau from Cocody, Treichville, Marcory and the port at Vridi. Lagoon transport is deeply embedded — traditional pinasse water-taxis and official Citrans/SOTRA boats move very large daily volumes where the road bridges are chronically congested — and the government has launched modern electric-boat pilots on the lagoon. It is a proven, high-volume water-commuter market ripe for a clean foiling upgrade.
why_marine_mobility: Abidjan is a city of ~6 million whose bridges are perpetually jammed while a calm, central lagoon carries the relief. Navier's Pioneer II flies the busiest crossings — Le Plateau to Treichville, Cocody and Vridi — silent and zero-emission, a premium upgrade over the diesel and pinasse fleet the city already depends on, while the Quanta-LR range opens coastal line-haul along the Gulf of Guinea to Grand-Bassam and beyond.

demand_signals.label: Ébrié Lagoon commuter volume
demand_signals.note: Lagoon boats carry very large daily passenger volumes across Abidjan, where the road bridges between Le Plateau, Cocody and the southern communes are chronically gridlocked.

demand_signals.label: Bridge-congestion bypass
demand_signals.note: With limited bridges spanning the lagoon, cross-water demand is structurally high — the lagoon is the only relief valve for a metro of ~6 million.

demand_signals.label: Plateau & Cocody waterfront
demand_signals.note: The Le Plateau business district and the upscale Cocody-Riviera waterfront concentrate high-value commuter and business demand on the lagoon edge.

use_cases.body: A clean, fast foiling tier across the busiest lagoon crossings — Le Plateau to Treichville, Marcory and Cocody — upgrading the diesel and pinasse fleet with silent, premium hops.
A port-and-airport connection down the lagoon from Le Plateau to Vridi and Port-Bouët, bypassing the congested southern road corridor.
Coastal leisure runs to the historic colonial town of Grand-Bassam on the Quanta-LR as range comes online.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The entire lagoon mesh — Le Plateau↔Treichville/Marcory (~1–1.5 nm), Plateau↔Cocody/Riviera (~2–3 nm), Plateau↔Yopougon (~5 nm), Plateau↔Vridi/Port-Bouët (~6 nm) — sits far inside the 70 nm all-electric range on calm, sheltered, flat lagoon water off existing landings.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The lagoon is pure Pioneer II territory; Quanta-LR hybrid range opens Gulf of Guinea coastal line-haul to Grand-Bassam (~18 nm) and Jacqueville (~22 nm) without charging build-out.

signature_routes.label: Abidjan Le Plateau ↔ Treichville / Marcory (all-electric lagoon crossing)

transit_planning: For the District of Abidjan, SOTRA or a private operator: a clean foiling tier on established lagoon landings, building directly on the government's own electric-boat modernisation of the Ébrié Lagoon and the app relationship of a ride-hail brand like Yango.
competitive_landscape: Abidjan has a mature lagoon-transport culture — informal pinasses, the municipal Citrans/SOTRA lagoon buses, and recently introduced electric passenger boats — all competing with chronically jammed road bridges. The water is trusted and heavily used; a foiling tier upgrades rather than creates demand.
regulatory_note: Lagoon transport is overseen by the District of Abidjan and national maritime/lagoon authorities, with SOTRA and licensed operators running official services. Côte d'Ivoire's own electric-boat initiative signals strong government appetite for clean lagoon modernisation, making the environment unusually receptive to a zero-emission foiling tier.
seasonality: The sheltered Ébrié Lagoon is calm and navigable year-round, giving a weather-stable commuter profile; the two rainy seasons (roughly April–July and October–November) bring heavier downpours but little sea-state disruption on the protected water, so the commuter network runs consistently.
